children.translated_text: I pay no heed to your virtues or faults — as is the enemy, so is the child, I know.

children.text: वचन कहत नहिं शंका तोहीं । कहे कठोर वचन बहु मोहीं ॥
children.translated_text: You speak these words without any fear; you have said many harsh words to me.

children.text: सो सुनि मोहिं क्रोधनहिं सपने । जाहु कुमार कुशल घरअपने ॥
children.translated_text: Hearing that, I feel not even a dream of anger — go home safely, O prince!

children.text: दो० अबलौं क्रोध न कीन मैं सुनो बीर बलवान ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: Until now I have shown no anger — listen, O mighty hero!

children.text: केहरिकेर स्वभाव नहिं बधिशृगाल खर श्वान ॥
children.translated_text: It is not the nature of a lion to slay jackals, donkeys, and dogs."

children.text: अस कहि भरत मौन ह्वै रहे । कुश मुसकाय बहुरिकुछकहे ॥
children.translated_text: Having said this, <s>Bharata</s> fell silent; <s>Kuśa</s> smiled and said something more.

children.text: सो सुनि भरतअधिकरिसमानी । बधों न तोहिंसुवनमुनिजानी ॥
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Bharata</s> grew angrier: "I do not slay you, knowing you to be a son of the forest and a sage.

children.text: ममता मोह तुरंग तजि भागो । अतिसुकुमार बीररस त्यागो ॥
children.translated_text: Abandon your attachment and affection for the horse and flee! You are far too delicate — give up the sentiment of valor.

children.text: शिशु बिचारि मैं बहुत सँणारा । निपटकालबशभयसि कुमारा ॥
children.translated_text: Considering you a child, I have shown much forbearance — but you are utterly in Death's grip, O prince!

children.text: तोहिं निपातमख तुरँगसमेता । जाउँ अवध जहँ कृपानिकेता ॥
children.translated_text: Slaying you, along with the sacrificial horse, I shall go to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, the abode of mercy.

children.text: यद्यपि अस विचार मन मोरे । करों न सांच विलोकत तोरे ॥
children.translated_text: Although such is the thought in my mind, looking at you, I cannot carry it out in truth."

children.text: कुश लौ हँसे सुनत रिपु बानी । मिला नरेश हमैं यह ज्ञानी ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Kuśa</s> laughed heartily hearing the enemy's words: "What a wise king we have encountered!

children.text: जो उपदेश न गुरुन बतावा ।सो हम आजु भूपसन पावा ॥
children.translated_text: The teaching that even our <s>Guru</s> never imparted, we have received today from this king!

children.text: बैर बिसारिलीन हय चाहा । सो गति यहां अगम नरनाहा ॥
children.translated_text: Forgetting enmity, you desire to take the horse — but that path is closed here, O king!

children.text: दो० आनों बोलि सहायकिमि बिधि हरि हरअमरेश ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: Even if you summon <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Indra</s> as allies,

children.text: जबलग तनपर शीश है मिलै न अश्व नरेश ॥
children.translated_text: as long as the head rests upon this body, you shall not obtain the horse, O king!"

children.text: असकहिसजगभये दोउभइया । सुमिरि मुनीपदपंकज मइया ॥
children.translated_text: Saying thus, the two brothers became alert, remembering the lotus-feet of the sage and their mother.

children.text: चापचढ़ाय हाथ में कीन्हा । भाथाबांधि बिषम शरलीन्हा ॥
children.translated_text: They strung their bows and took them in hand, fastened their quivers and drew terrible arrows.

children.text: पाछे तुरँग राखिभे ठाढ़े । महाबली हथियारन गाढ़े ॥
children.translated_text: They stood behind with the horse, those mighty warriors, firmly gripping their weapons.

children.text: युद्ध विरुद्ध देखि दोउ बीरा । सहमे भरत भूप रणधीरा ॥
children.translated_text: Seeing the two heroes poised for battle, even the battle-steadfast King <s>Bharata</s> was shaken.

children.text: लगे विचार करन अवनीशा । ये न सुवनऋषिराज मुनीशा ॥
children.translated_text: The lord of the earth began to ponder: "These are not mere forest-dwelling sons of a sage-king.

children.text: अवशि राजबन्शी हैं दोऊ । अस शोभानहिं जगमेंकोऊ ॥
children.translated_text: Surely both belong to a royal lineage — such splendor is found in no one else in the world.

children.text: मुनिवर वेष बसैं बनमाहीं । छबिनिधानलखिकामलजाहीं ॥
children.translated_text: Though they dwell in the forest in the garb of sages, seeing their beauty, even <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love) would be put to shame.

children.text: रिपुसुदन मदभंजन हारा । नींह कोउ बीर सकल संसारा ॥
children.translated_text: Slayers of foes, destroyers of pride — there are no warriors like these in the entire world.

children.text: तेज पुंज अतिशय दिखराई । मनहुं संग सैना समुदाई ॥
children.translated_text: Their radiance is extraordinary, blazing forth, as though an entire army were assembled with them."

children.text: सो० बिन कीन्हे संग्राम हाथ न लागै तुरँग मख ।
children.translated_text: Sorṭhā: Without fighting a battle, the sacrificial horse cannot be obtained;

children.text: अस बिचारिबलधाम कोपिलीन धनुबानकर ॥
children.translated_text: thinking thus, that abode of strength seized bow and arrow in anger.

children.text: भुजा उठाय पुकारे योधा । आये जहँ तहँ सैन सक्रोधा ।
children.translated_text: Raising his arms, the warrior called out; soldiers came from every direction, wrathful.

children.text: कुशबिलोकि रिपुसैन समूहा । आये चहुँदिशि युत्थनजूहा ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Kuśa</s>, seeing the enemy's assembled forces approaching from all four directions in battle-formations,

children.text: लवहि सौंपि मुरचा भटभारी । सन्मुख राजन आप सिधारी ॥
children.translated_text: entrusted the heavy battle-mace to <s>Lava</s> and himself advanced toward the king.

children.text: कुश अरुभरतदोऊ बलधामा । लड़ैं प्रचारि भूमिसंग्रामा ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Bharata</s>, both abodes of strength, fought fiercely in ground combat.

children.text: दुहुँ दिशिचलैं बाण अतितीछे । भूल्यो कोउ पग धरै न पीछे ॥
children.translated_text: Exceedingly sharp arrows flew from both sides — no one was confused, no one stepped back.

children.text: शरन भये तन झांझर दोऊ । तदपि न हटैं बीर रण कोऊ ॥
children.translated_text: Both their bodies became riddled with arrows like sieves, yet neither hero retreated from battle.

children.text: धनुषबाण डास्यो यकसाथा । भिरे दोऊ कृपान लै हाथा ॥
children.translated_text: Both cast aside their bows and arrows together, and closed in with swords in hand.

children.text: सुनहु खगेश काकपति कहही । दोउ अघाय बल शरतररहही ॥
children.translated_text: Listen, O lord of birds, says the lord of crows: both fought insatiably with the might of their arrows and swords.

children.text: जूझे सुभट रहे जे संगा । परे भूमि रणशोणित अंगा ॥
children.translated_text: The fine warriors who had accompanied them fell in battle, their bodies drenched in blood upon the earth.

children.text: छन्द ॥
children.translated_text: Chanda:

children.text: परे भूमि शोणित अंग भट बहु रुधिर के नारे बहे ।
children.translated_text: Warriors fell upon the earth, limbs bloodied, streams of gore flowed forth,

children.text: डरपे सुरासुर देखिरण गये भाग नहिं कोउ थिर रहे ॥
children.translated_text: gods and demons were terrified seeing the battle — all fled, none could stand firm.

children.text: बहु गिद्ध श्वान शृगाल केहरि मुदित भोजन पायकै ।
children.translated_text: Many vultures, dogs, jackals, and lions rejoiced, having found their feast;

children.text: बैताल भूत पिशाच योगिनि पियें रुधिर अघायकै ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Vetālas</s>, ghosts, <s>piśācas</s>, and <s>yoginīs</s> drank blood to their fill.

children.text: कट कटहिं एकहि एक घोर कठोरकहि भय दिखावहीं ।
children.translated_text: They gnash their teeth at one another, uttering terrible and harsh words to strike fear;

children.text: नाचैं बजावैं ताल गति रण राग सुन्दर गावहीं ॥
children.translated_text: they dance and clap rhythm, singing beautiful battle-melodies in the field of war.

children.text: संग्राम महि दोउ बीर कोपे तमकि धनुशायक गहा ।
children.translated_text: On the battlefield, the two heroes, enraged, furiously seized bows and arrows;

children.text: भये विकल जीव सचेत सब नहिं धीर त्यहि औसररहा ॥
children.translated_text: all living beings became distraught — not a single one remained composed at that moment.

children.text: सो० समर भरत कुशवीर देखा सुना न अस कहूं ।
children.translated_text: Sorṭhā: The battle between <s>Bharata</s> and the hero <s>Kuśa</s> — such a fight was never seen nor heard of anywhere.

children.text: भरद्वाज मुनि धीर सुनो कह्यो जाबालि अस ॥
children.translated_text: The steadfast sage <s>Bharadvāja</s> — listen — thus spoke <s>Jābāli</s>.

children.text: वहां सुभट सब लौ संहारे । बहे अनेक रुधिर नद नारे ॥
children.translated_text: Meanwhile all the fine warriors were slain; many rivers of blood flowed forth.

children.text: तब लौ अनुजओर त्यहिकाला । दै ललकार लड़ै महिपाला ॥
children.translated_text: At that very time, the younger brother (<s>Lava</s>) on the other side challenged and fought the kings.

children.text: बड़ीभीर कुश ऊपर जाना । शरसन्धानचल्यो बलवाना ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Kuśa</s>, seeing great peril upon himself, the mighty one set arrows to string and advanced.

children.text: दूरहि से बोले लौ बीरा । आये पुनि जहँ कुश रणधीरा ॥
children.translated_text: The hero <s>Lava</s> called out from a distance, then came again to where the battle-steadfast <s>Kuśa</s> was.

children.text: दीख अनुज कहँ पीछे ठाढ़ा । लागे लड़ै अधिक बलबाढ़ा ॥
children.translated_text: Seeing his younger brother standing behind, he fought on with even greater force.

children.text: बाण प्रहार भूप रथ तोपी । समरअजरदोउअतिशयकोपी ॥
children.translated_text: With a volley of arrows <s>Kuśa</s> smashed the king's chariot — both combatants were exceedingly wrathful, unwearied in battle.

children.text: उमा भरत सम बीर न कोउ । सकै न आज जीत रणसोऊ ॥
children.translated_text: O <s>Umā</s>, there is no hero equal to <s>Bharata</s>, yet even he could not win the battle that day.

children.text: जबहिं कोपि कुश छाँड्योबाना । चुभ्योभरततनब्यालसमाना ॥
children.translated_text: When <s>Kuśa</s> in fury released an arrow, it pierced <s>Bharata</s>'s body like a serpent.

children.text: लागत बाण भयो उर पीरा । परे मुरछि स्यन्दन बर बीरा ॥
children.translated_text: As the arrow struck, great pain arose in his chest; the noble hero fell unconscious on his chariot.

children.text: दो० देखि दशा भागे सुभट बचे जे जीवत खेत ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: Seeing this state, the surviving warriors who remained alive on the battlefield fled,

children.text: जाय पुकारे ते सभी जहँ प्रभु लषण समेत ॥
children.translated_text: and they all went crying out to where the Lord was, along with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: शोणित अंग त्रास उर भारी । जय अवधपुर कीन्ह पुकारी ॥
children.translated_text: With blood-soaked limbs and great terror in their hearts, they raised the cry "Victory to <s>Ayodhyā</s>!"

children.text: मुरछित भरतसचिवसुनिकाना । भयोबिकलनहिंजायबखाना ॥
children.translated_text: When the minister heard that <s>Bharata</s> lay unconscious, he became so distraught it cannot be described.

children.text: पुनि धरिधीर तुरितचलिआयो । भरतदशा रघुबरहि सुनायो ॥
children.translated_text: Then, gathering courage, he came swiftly and reported <s>Bharata</s>'s condition to <s>Raghuvara</s> (<s>Rāma</s>).

children.text: सकल समाजसहित रघुराई । सचिववचनसुनिरहेअरगाई ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Raghurāī</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) along with his entire court, hearing the minister's words, remained stunned.

children.text: बिकलभईं सुनिसुनि सबमाता । कहा बिरञ्चिकीन्ह उतपाता ॥
children.translated_text: All the queens became distressed hearing the news again and again: "What calamity has <s>Brahmā</s> wrought!"

children.text: पुरवासी सब अतिअकुलाने । सुनेहुजोजहांतहां बिलखाने ॥
children.translated_text: All the city-dwellers were greatly agitated; wherever people heard, they lamented.

children.text: पुरजन शोच शोच बश जानी । गुरुबशिष्ठ बोले मृदुबानी ॥
children.translated_text: Knowing the people were overcome with grief, the <s>Guru</s> <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> spoke gentle words:

children.text: तुम सर्वज्ञ ईश रघुराया । तुमहिं न सपन्योव्यापीमाया ॥
children.translated_text: "You are omniscient, O Lord <s>Raghurāyā</s> — <s>Māyā</s> (illusion) cannot touch you even in a dream.

children.text: धरहु धीर असकह्यो मुनीशा । कीजै काज यज्ञअवधेशा ॥
children.translated_text: Be steadfast" — thus spoke the chief of sages — "carry on the work of the sacrifice, O Lord of <s>Ayodhyā</s>."

children.text: सो० सुनहु मुनीश सुजान घरो धीर करुणाअयन ।
children.translated_text: Sorṭhā: "Listen, O wise lord of sages, be firm, O abode of compassion;

children.text: विधिगतिलखिबलवान समुझिबुलायेअनुजलघु ।
children.translated_text: perceiving the workings of fate, that mighty one, reflecting, summoned his younger brother."

children.text: लक्ष्मणकहँ प्रभु तुरित बुलाई । हृदय लगाय निकट बैठाई ॥
children.translated_text: The Lord quickly summoned <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, embraced him to his heart, and seated him nearby.

children.text: बोले सरल मनोहर बानी । दीनदयालसुनहु मुनिज्ञानी ॥
children.translated_text: He spoke in simple and charming words: "O merciful to the distressed, listen, O knower of sages' ways:

children.text: साजि सैन यहि औसर जाई । देखो कहँ जूझे दोउ भाई ॥
children.translated_text: Prepare an army and go at once — see where the two brothers have fallen in battle.

children.text: रिपुसूदन भारत रिपु पाई । हत रणखेत अश्व मखलाई ॥
children.translated_text: The slayer of foes, <s>Bharata</s>, encountering the enemy, has been struck down on the battlefield, and the sacrificial horse has been taken.

children.text: जो निज जान्यो कुवँरऋषेशा । कियो न रणतिनसंगफणीशा ॥
children.translated_text: If you judge them to be princes of a sage-lord, then do not fight them, O <s>Śeṣanāga</s> (Serpent Lord).

children.text: जो क्षत्रीकर वेष छिपाये । फिरैं विपिन मुनि वेष बनाये ॥
children.translated_text: If they are <s>Kṣatriyas</s> who have concealed their identity, roaming the forest disguised as sages,

children.text: करब समर नहिं करब अबारी । आन्यहुबेग तुरँग बलिहारी ॥
children.translated_text: then do battle, do not hold back — bring the horse swiftly, I entreat you!"

children.text: सुनिलक्ष्मण आयसु अवधेशा । चले नाय पदंपकज शीशा ॥
children.translated_text: Hearing the command of the Lord of <s>Ayodhyā</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> departed, bowing his head at the lotus-feet.

children.text: लीन सैन चतुरंग भवानी । जे सपनेहु रणहारि न मानी ॥
children.translated_text: He took along the four-fold army, O <s>Bhavānī</s> — those who had never acknowledged defeat even in dreams.

children.text: दो० पहिर विविध सन्नाह सब शूल शक्तिलै हाथ ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: Donning various armors, all grasping spears and lances in hand,

children.text: सन्मुख श्रीरघुनाथके सादर नावहिं माथ ॥
children.translated_text: they reverently bowed their heads before Śrī <s>Raghunātha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>).

children.text: तब लक्ष्मण बोले कर जोरी । बाणी मधुर सुधारस बोरी ॥
children.translated_text: Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> spoke with folded hands, his words sweet and drenched in nectar:

children.text: जो करिकपट भूपसुत कोऊ । करहिं ठगी बनमें बसिदोऊ ॥
children.translated_text: "If some king's sons have practiced deceit, and the two dwell in the forest as impostors,

children.text: तो बध करब न वेष बिचारों । तुरंग समेत निकेत सिधारों ॥
children.translated_text: then I shall slay them without regard for their garb and return home with the horse.

children.text: जो मुनीशसुत आहैं दोऊ । तो जस आयसुसाहब होऊ ॥
children.translated_text: But if they are sons of a great sage, then let whatever be the Lord's command, so be it —

children.text: तस मैं करों जाय बन माहीं । अनुचितकहिनसकोंप्रभुपाहीं ॥
children.translated_text: that I shall do, going into the forest; I cannot say anything improper before my Lord."

children.text: सुनि रघुनाथ विनय लघुभ्राता । बोले विहँसि मधुरमृदुबाता ॥
children.translated_text: Hearing the humble words of his younger brother, <s>Raghunātha</s> smiled and spoke sweet, gentle words:

children.text: सुनो तात तुम परमविवेकी । का न कहो परमारथ टेकी ॥
children.translated_text: "Listen, dear one, you are supremely wise — why do you not speak to the ultimate truth?

children.text: सोई करब मिलै जेहि बाजू । आनभांति सबहोय अकाजू ॥
children.translated_text: We must do whatever brings back the horse; any other course will lead to ruin."

children.text: गहि 'पद कंज मंजु रघुराई । लक्ष्ममणचल्योसभाशिरनाई ॥
children.translated_text: Clasping the beautiful lotus-feet of <s>Raghurāī</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> departed, bowing before the assembly.

children.text: दो॰ सुमिरशिवाशिव चढ़योरथ सन्मुख सैनचलाय ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: Remembering <s>Śivā</s> and <s>Śiva</s>, he mounted his chariot and set the army marching forward,

children.text: बार बार संभारि उर पदपंकज रघुराय ॥
children.translated_text: again and again holding in his heart the lotus-feet of <s>Raghurāya</s>.

children.text: चली कटक लक्ष्मण खगनाहू । सैना प्रबल त्रास नहिं काहू ॥
children.translated_text: The army of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> marched forth, O lord of birds — a mighty force, with none feeling any fear.

children.text: सुभट न भार धरा कुर्मकाँपू । मेरु चूर भे हय गज टापू ॥
children.translated_text: The earth could not bear the weight of those warriors, the tortoise trembled; mountains were crushed under the hooves of horses and elephants.

children.text: करहिं कोलाहल भट मगजाता । आगे यान राम लघुभ्राता ॥
children.translated_text: The warriors raised a clamor along the road; at the front rode <s>Rāma</s>'s younger brother in his chariot.

children.text: निकट विपिन रिपु आये जबहीं । बोलेबचनलषण असतबहीं ॥
children.translated_text: When they drew near the forest where the enemy was, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> spoke these words:

children.text: ह्वै सब मौन फिरहु बनजाई । लेहु खोज हयरिपु दोउभाई ॥
children.translated_text: "All of you, be silent and go through the forest — search for the horse and the two enemy brothers.

children.text: देख्यो जहां न बोल्यो भाई । शब्दआयमोहिं कह्यो सुनाई ॥
children.translated_text: Wherever you spot them, do not speak, brothers — bring word and report to me.

children.text: तब मैं विपिन घेरि चहुँओरा । सहजै बांधि लेउँ हयचोरा ॥
children.translated_text: Then I shall surround the forest on all sides and easily capture the horse-thieves."

children.text: असकहिकीन्ह बिदा सबबीरा । बीरधुरीण लषण रणधीरा ॥
children.translated_text: Having said this, the foremost among heroes, the battle-steadfast <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, dismissed all the warriors.

children.text: सुभट जबहिं बन पैठन लागे । कसमसात पगपरै न आगे ॥
children.translated_text: When the warriors began to enter the forest, they shuddered — their feet could not move forward.

children.text: छन्द ॥
children.translated_text: Chanda:

children.text: पगपरै न आगे सुभट के लखि सघन बन भारी महा ।
children.translated_text: The warriors' feet would not advance, seeing the dense and terribly thick forest;

children.text: यकएक बीधुरीण समरथ धीर नहिं कोऊ रहा ॥
children.translated_text: one by one, even the foremost brave and resolute warriors lost their nerve.

children.text: निज नाथ काज बिचारि जिय पर तेज बन बैठीसही ।
children.translated_text: Reflecting in their hearts on their master's purpose, they endured, though the forest's might pressed upon them;

children.text: तेहिसमय सैना बिकलता नहिं जात कछु मोसों कही ॥
children.translated_text: the distress of the army at that time — I cannot express it in words.

children.text: सो० जानि रामको काज तापर आयसु लक्ष्मण ।
children.translated_text: Sorṭhā: Knowing it to be <s>Rāma</s>'s task, and moreover having <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s command,

children.text: खोजनलागे बाज जहँ तहँ बन में पैठि सब ॥
children.translated_text: they began searching for the horse, entering the forest here and there, all of them.

children.text: दो० सकलविपिन यकओरते चले सुभट सुधिलेत ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: From one end of the entire forest, the warriors advanced, seeking intelligence;

children.text: कहूं न पायो अन्त हय दोऊ कुवँर समेत ॥
children.translated_text: nowhere did they find any trace of the horse or the two princes.

children.text: हेरत विपिन फिरत कटकाई । कहूं खोज मखबाजि न पाई ॥
children.translated_text: Searching through the forest, the army wandered — nowhere was any trace of the sacrificial horse found.

children.text: ठाढ़ परस्पर सब पछिताहीं । रामराम कहि कहँ अबजाहीं ॥
children.translated_text: Standing together, all regretted: "<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Rāma</s>!" they cried — "Where do we go now?

children.text: जो बिनखोज तुरँग अबजाई । कौनबदन लक्ष्मणहिं दिखाई ॥
children.translated_text: If we return now without finding the horse, with what face can we appear before <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>?"

children.text: नहिंसुधिभोजनअरुजलपाना । फिरहिंविपिनसबयथाअयाना ॥
children.translated_text: There was no thought of food or water; they wandered through the forest aimlessly.

children.text: तेहिमा एक सुभट बिलगाई । गयो जहां बन टेढ़ सुहाई ॥
children.translated_text: Among them, one warrior strayed apart and went to where the forest path wound beautifully.

children.text: तहां देखि सुन्दर मुनिबागा । तरु रमाल नवपल्लव लागा ॥
children.translated_text: There he beheld a lovely sage's garden, with rows of trees bearing fresh foliage.

children.text: सुरपतिबाग न पटतर आवा । तुरँगसमेत चोर हय पावा ॥
children.translated_text: Even <s>Indra</s>'s garden could not compare; along with the horse, he found the horse-thieves.

children.text: चेल्यो तुरतलक्ष्मण के पासा । जानिविपिनहयचोरनिवासा ॥
children.translated_text: He hurried at once to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s side, having found the horse-thieves' dwelling in the forest.

children.text: मिले सकल भटसुभट निहारी । पूंछन लागे खबरि सुखारी ॥
children.translated_text: All the warriors gathered, seeing the fine soldier, and began asking for the welcome news.

children.text: दो० मुदितभये सुधिपाय हय सहित चोर बनमांझ ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: They rejoiced upon learning the whereabouts of the horse along with the thieves in the forest;

children.text: सीध चले लक्ष्ममण जहां गयो दिवस भै सांझ ॥
children.translated_text: they marched straight to where <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> was — the day had ended and evening had come.

children.text: लक्ष्मण आय चरण शिरनाई । सुधि मखबाजिकह्योहरषाई ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> came and bowed his head at the feet, and joyfully reported the news of the sacrificial horse:

children.text: महा टेढ़ बन नाथ सुहाई । भानुप्रताप न सपनेहुजाई ॥
children.translated_text: "My lord, there is a great and winding, beautiful forest — even the sun's radiance cannot enter it in dreams.

children.text: देखातहँ यक मुनि फुलवारी । बाजिसहितदोउचोरनिहारी ॥
children.translated_text: There we saw a sage's flower-garden, and beheld the two thieves along with the horse.

children.text: पन्थन गजरथ हय रथ शेखा । पातपात सब बनहमदेखा ॥
children.translated_text: On the paths we saw elephants, chariots, horses, and their remains — at every step we saw the forest (littered with wreckage).

children.text: सत्यबचन सुनिसुभट अनन्ता । सजगकह्योभटबोलितुरन्ता ॥
children.translated_text: Hearing those true words, the countless warriors became alert; the soldiers were told and spoke in haste.

children.text: निज स्यन्दन साहनी पुकारी । चढ़ेतुरँग लक्ष्मण बलधारी ॥
children.translated_text: Calling his own charioteer, the mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> mounted his horse.

children.text: चतुरंगिणी अनी समुदाई । कछु आगे कछु पाछे जाई ॥
children.translated_text: The four-fold army assembled — some went ahead, some followed behind.

children.text: करिआगे सोसुभट भवानी । जिनबनशोधि अश्वसुधिआनी ॥
children.translated_text: At the front was placed that warrior, O <s>Bhavānī</s>, who had searched the forest and brought news of the horse.

children.text: कसमसात भट मारग जाहीं । भ्रमबश चौंक देखिपरछाहीं ॥
children.translated_text: The warriors shuddered as they went along the path, startled by illusion, jumping at their own shadows.

children.text: छन्द ॥
children.translated_text: Chanda:

children.text: चौंकैं सुभट बन पात खड़कत पांवनहिं आगे परैं ।
children.translated_text: The warriors flinch at the rustling of leaves in the forest; their feet will not step forward.

children.text: जेपाय अधजीवन बिपिन छिनचलेंछिन फनफनकरैं ॥
children.translated_text: Those who found themselves half-alive in the forest — one moment they advanced, the next they hissed with terror.

children.text: अकुलाय भट पछिताय तहँवाँ देव इष्ट मनावहीं ।
children.translated_text: The agitated warriors, full of regret, prayed there to their chosen deities;

children.text: चेरे लषण सैना सहित पुरचलैं तहँ फिर आवहीं ॥
children.translated_text: servants of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, along with the army — they would march toward the city, then turn back again.

children.text: सो० भय बश भे सब बीर देखि बिपिन हास्यो हिये ।
children.translated_text: Sorṭhā: All the warriors were overcome with fear; seeing the forest, they laughed inwardly (at their own plight).

children.text: लक्ष्मण से रणधीर काको आनि गिनाइये ॥
children.translated_text: But who can be compared to one as battle-steadfast as <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>?

children.text: दो० शारदूल के नाद सुनि जहँ तहँ सुभट डेराहिं ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: Hearing the roar of tigers, the warriors trembled here and there;

children.text: मारग में कसमस भई बिना जीव सब जाहिं ॥
children.translated_text: on the road there was such dread that they walked as though lifeless.

children.text: खड़खड़ाहिं शूकर सुनि चालू । पिहँकैं गज ठहुकैं कपिभालू ॥
children.translated_text: Wild boars crashed and clattered; elephants trumpeted, monkeys and bears bellowed;

children.text: केहरि नाद चहूं दिशि होई । महा सघन बन जाय न जोई ॥
children.translated_text: lions roared on all four sides — the forest was so dense one could not see through it.

children.text: काँपे उर लक्ष्मण रणधीरा । श्रमित शत्रुजसहोयअधीरा ॥
children.translated_text: Even the battle-steadfast <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s heart trembled; wearied, the foe-conqueror grew uneasy.

children.text: सम्मित तजी बीरता भारी । जनुठगजीहलीन्ह ज्योंमारी ॥
children.translated_text: His great heroism seemed to desert him, as though a thief had robbed him of his very life-breath.

children.text: रहा न तेज न दृढ़ परकाशा । तजी सबन जीवनकी आशा ॥
children.translated_text: Neither radiance nor firm resolve remained; all abandoned hope of survival.

children.text: घेरिलीन चारो दिशि बागा । बाद बिनोद होन पुनिलागा ॥
children.translated_text: They surrounded and enclosed the garden on all four sides; then a wondrous exchange began to unfold.

children.text: लव को राखि अश्व रखवारी । कुश सन्मुख ह्वै नृपललकारी ॥
children.translated_text: Leaving <s>Lava</s> to guard the horse, <s>Kuśa</s> advanced and challenged the king:

children.text: को तुम कहो कहां ते आवो । बाहर रहो न बाग मँझावो ॥
children.translated_text: "Who are you? Say — where have you come from? Stay outside; do not enter the garden!"

children.text: दो० अस कहि चाप चढ़ाय कुश बोले बचन सकोपि ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: Saying this, <s>Kuśa</s> strung his bow and spoke wrathful words;

children.text: कसी चारि बढ़ि तुरँग से भे ठाढ़े पद रोपि ॥
children.translated_text: he tightened his belt, advanced like a horse (in swiftness), and stood firm, feet planted.

children.text: ललकारे बाजै असवारा । को तुम यहां कहां पगधारा ॥
children.translated_text: He challenged the horseman: "Who are you here? Where have you set foot?

children.text: बैरि जानि ताते कटकाई । अति निशंक आवेंफुलवाई ॥
children.translated_text: I know you as enemies — that is why your army has come so fearlessly into this flower-garden.

children.text: देखि भीर सेना सँग भारी । मैं जाना कहुं अन्त सिधारी ॥
children.translated_text: Seeing the heavy press of forces with you, I understood that some expedition has arrived.

children.text: सो अरुझे तुम हमसनआई । कहांकुशल नृप कहोसुनाई ॥
children.translated_text: So you have come and entangled yourselves with us! Tell me, O king, what news of your welfare?

children.text: फरक रहो जनि पैठो बागा । हमहिंतुमहिंअबलागीलागा ॥
children.translated_text: Do not boast; do not enter the garden — between you and us, a quarrel has now begun!"

children.text: अससुनिलषण रोंकि हयराखा । योधन सों अपनेअसभाखा ॥
children.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> halted the horse and spoke thus to his warriors:

children.text: रहोठाढ जहँ तहँ सब बीरा । रिपुबललखिजनिहोहुअधीरा ॥
children.translated_text: "Stand firm, all you heroes, wherever you are — seeing the enemy's strength, do not lose heart.

children.text: जो आपुहि हय देहिं मँगाई । तौनउचितसँगकरियलड़ाई ॥
children.translated_text: If they give us the horse when asked, then it is not proper to do battle.

children.text: जो कछु बल पौरुषलखिपाई । तो बांधो हय लेहु छड़ाई ॥
children.translated_text: But if you find any show of strength and valor, then bind them and seize the horse by force!"

children.text: दो० रामअनुज बाणी बिमल सुनि हरषे सब बीर ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: Hearing the pure words of <s>Rāma</s>'s younger brother, all the warriors rejoiced;

children.text: सजे समर हथियार भट खड़े बाग के तीर ॥
children.translated_text: the soldiers readied their weapons for battle and stood at the edge of the garden.

children.text: कह्योलषण सुनिऋषयकुमारा । कस बांध्यो तुमअश्वहमारा ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> spoke, addressing the sage's sons: "Why have you bound our horse?

children.text: तुरँग बांधि करि पौरुष भारी । भारत रिपुसूदन रणमारी ॥
children.translated_text: Having bound the horse with great display of valor, you struck down <s>Bharata</s>, the foe-slayer, in battle.

children.text: कौन मोह बाजै परतोहीं । मूरख कटुकवचन कहेमोहीं ॥
children.translated_text: What infatuation has come over you regarding this horse? Fool, you have spoken harsh words to me!

children.text: मैं पुनि नीति समुझिमनमाहीं । अबलग क्रोधकीन उरनाहीं ॥
children.translated_text: Yet I, reflecting on what is right in my mind, have not shown anger until now.

children.text: अबहूँ कुशल तुरँगमोहिं दीजै । मुदितपयानभवननिजकीजै ॥
children.translated_text: Even now, give me the horse and you shall be well — depart joyfully to your own home.

children.text: देखि वेष मुनिबर दोउ बीरा । रास्यों रोंकि सुभटरणधीरा ॥
children.translated_text: Seeing the garb of sages upon you two heroes, I have held back, restraining the warriors.

children.text: सो तुम नहिं मुनिबालक दोऊ । शोभा अमित भूपसुत कोऊ ॥
children.translated_text: But you are not mere sage-children — your splendor is boundless; you must be princes of some king."

children.text: तुमसेन निडर कहां मुनिजाये । अस रण तेज कहांउनपाये ॥
children.translated_text: Where have you sage-born ones learned such fearlessness? Where did you obtain such battle-prowess?

children.text: कछुअपराध कीन्ह तुम भारी । सो बिचारि पितुदीननिकारी ॥
children.translated_text: You have committed some great offense; considering that, your father cast you out as wretched.

children.text: दो० धनुषबाण बांधे फिरौ ऋषिमुनि वेष बनाय ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: You roam about with bow and arrows, disguised in the garb of sages and ascetics,

children.text: करहुविपिनबसिदिवसनिशि मोहविवशअन्याय ॥
children.translated_text: dwelling in the forest day and night, committing injustice under the spell of delusion.

children.text: अप्रिय बचनलषण कछु भाखे । सोसुनिअधिककुवँरदोउमाखे ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> spoke some harsh and unpleasant words; hearing them, both princes grew even more furious.

children.text: भे सरोष दोउ बन्धु बिशेखी । बोले बचन भूपदिशि देखी ॥
children.translated_text: Both brothers became wrathful and agitated, and spoke these words while looking toward the king's direction:

children.text: कहत बचन लघु शोभा नाहीं । देखो नृप विचारि मनमाहीं ॥
children.translated_text: "Speaking petty words brings no glory — consider this well in your mind, O king.

children.text: सो नहिं शोच हमैं कछु राजा । जोतुमकहहुतुमहिंसबछाजा ॥
children.translated_text: We have no concern at all for that, O king; what you say befits only you.

children.text: करहु बिलम कस रचहु उपाई । मारि हमैं हयलेहु छुड़ाई ॥
children.translated_text: Why do you delay? Devise some stratagem — slay us and take the horse freed!

children.text: जग अस बीर कहां सुनुराजा । हमको जीति जायलै बाजा ॥
children.translated_text: Where in the world is there such a warrior, listen O king, who could defeat us and take the horse?

children.text: ब्रह्म विष्णु शंकर से गाढ़े । सो सन्मुख रणहोहिं न ठाढ़े ॥
children.translated_text: Even those mighty as <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śaṅkara</s> would not stand before us in battle.

children.text: तहां कौन पुरुषारथ आना । जाहुकुशल भूपतिबलवाना ॥
children.translated_text: What valor can anyone else display? Go safely, O mighty king!

children.text: जो पै मरण समर जिय ठानी । होहुसजग नृपसुनिममबानी ॥
children.translated_text: But if you have resolved to die in battle, then be alert, O king — hear my words!"

children.text: सो० असकहि दोउ रणधीर धनुषचढ़ाय सिधार शर ।
children.translated_text: Sorthā: Thus spoke both warriors, steadfast in battle, stringing their bows and readying their arrows,

children.text: जहां अनुज रघुबीर पहुंचे सन्मुख जाय तब ॥
children.translated_text: and went to where the younger brother of <s>Raghu's</s> hero stood, arriving face to face.

children.text: लक्ष्मण देखि सरुष दोउबीरा । चाप बाण कटि कसे तुणीरा ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> beheld both warriors in fury, with bows and arrows and quivers fastened at their waists,

children.text: काल समान ठाढ़ दोउ आगे । मानों जीव चहत लै भागे ॥
children.translated_text: standing before him like Death incarnate, as if Life itself wished to flee.

children.text: यदपि अत्यन्त महा भटमानी । तदपि न धीरज रहाभवानी ॥
children.translated_text: Though he was an exceedingly great and proud warrior, even so his composure did not hold, O <s>Bhavānī</s>.

children.text: कछु धीरज धरि आप सँभारी । बोले बचन समय अनुहारी ॥
children.translated_text: Gathering some courage and composing himself, he spoke words befitting the occasion:

children.text: हमहिं तुमहिं कतसोह लड़ाई । अबहुँ कुशल हय देहुमंगाई ॥
children.translated_text: "What glory is there in fighting between us? Even now, return the horse peacefully."

children.text: सुनत वचन तमके दोउ भाई । रेमहीप त्वहिं लाज न आई ॥
children.translated_text: Hearing these words, both brothers flared with rage: "O prince of the earth, have you no shame?

children.text: जबलग जीव रहै घट माहीं । तबलग अश्व देब नृपानाहीं ॥
children.translated_text: As long as life remains in our bodies, we shall never give up the horse, O king!

children.text: हाथ जोरि पदत्राण निकारी । सन्मुख विनती करहु हमारी ॥
children.translated_text: Join your hands, remove your footwear, and make supplication before us.

children.text: जो कदापि हमरे जिय आवे । तो कहुं तुरंग भूप तैं पावे ॥
children.translated_text: If ever it should please our hearts, then perhaps you might receive the horse from us, O king."

children.text: दो० ऐसे अनुचित वचनबहु कहा जबै दोउ बीर ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: When both warriors spoke such many improper words,

children.text: भयो क्रोध सुनि लषणके बोले गिरा गँभीर ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> grew wrathful upon hearing them and spoke in a deep, grave voice:

children.text: रे बालकहु अबूझ अयाना । लखिस्वरूपमुखबचनसयाना ॥
children.translated_text: "O foolish, ignorant children! By your appearance and face you seem wise, but your words betray you.

children.text: मैं त्वहिंमुनिबर तनय बिचारी । अबलग बहुतै क्रोध सँभारी ॥
children.translated_text: I have restrained my great anger until now, considering you sons of a sage.

children.text: अब न तजोंशठतोहिंयहिकाला । मारि भूमि रणकरों बिहाला ॥
children.translated_text: But now I shall not spare you, wretches, at this very moment — I shall strike you down and leave you desolate on the battlefield.

children.text: शप्त मोहिं कोशलपुर भूपा । अजितअनामयअगुणअरूपा ॥
children.translated_text: I swear by the king of <s>Kosalapura</s> — unconquered, unblemished, beyond qualities, formless —

children.text: देखत तोहिं लेउँ मख घोड़ा । जाउँअवध शठसुनुप्रणमोरा ॥
children.translated_text: before your eyes I shall take the sacrificial horse and go to <s>Ayodhyā</s> — hear my vow, wretches!

children.text: हम क्षत्री क्षत्रीसन लड़हीं । द्विजमुनिवरऋषितापसडरहीं ॥
children.translated_text: We are <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and fight with <s>Kṣatriyas</s>; we are wary of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, sages, seers, and ascetics.

children.text: सो तुम नहिं मुनिबालक दोऊ । रूप छिपाय भूपकुल कोऊ ॥
children.translated_text: But you two are not sage-children — you are some princes disguising your identity!"

children.text: इतना कहत लषण रणधीरा । सजग भये दृगपुलकशरीरा ॥
children.translated_text: Having said this much, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, that steadfast warrior, became alert, his eyes moist and body thrilling with horripilation.

children.text: मुख अनुहार देखि अवधीशा । लागे करन विचार फणीशा ॥
children.translated_text: Looking at their facial resemblance to the lord of <s>Ayodhyā</s>, O <s>Śeṣanāga</s>, he began to reflect.

children.text: दो० कहांतनय अस ढीठमुनि रहैं ठाढ़ शर जोर ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: "Where have such bold sons of a sage been seen, standing with arrows drawn?

children.text: छाया रघुबर बदनकी देख कहत मन भोर ॥
children.translated_text: I see the shadow of <s>Raghuvara's</s> face in them," he said, his mind bewildered.

children.text: यहि बन बसत कहूं वैदेही । सुवन प्रताप बली ये तेही ॥
children.translated_text: "Could <s>Vaidehī</s> be dwelling somewhere in this forest? These valiant ones may be her mighty sons."

children.text: असकहि प्रभुआयसुअनुमाना । सुभट बुलाय कह्योबलवाना ॥
children.translated_text: Thinking thus, the Lord made an estimation, and calling his warriors, the mighty one commanded:

children.text: जियत धरहु दूनों कहँ जाई । बांधि कुवँर हय लेहु छुड़ाई ॥
children.translated_text: "Go and capture both of them alive — bind the princes and free the horse!"

children.text: अससुनिसुभटचले त्यहिओरा । करिमृगनाद महाअतिघोरा ॥
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the warriors marched in that direction, roaring terribly like wild beasts.

children.text: लीन घेर चहुंदिशि मुनिबागू । अति सभीत पगपरैनआगू ॥
children.translated_text: They surrounded the sage's garden on all four sides; greatly frightened, none dared step forward.

children.text: कुश विलोकि सैना रिपुआई । विहँसिशरासनतुरिन चढ़ाई ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Kuśa</s>, seeing the enemy army approach, smiled and instantly strung his bow.

children.text: शत शत बाण जोरि यकसाथा । मास्यो सुभटन उरभुजमाथा ॥
children.translated_text: Shooting hundreds of arrows at once, he struck the warriors on their chests, arms, and heads.

children.text: लवनिप्रमाण सुभट सब छीजे । देखिदशा लक्ष्मण तबखीजे ॥
children.translated_text: In an instant, <s>Lava</s> cut down all the warriors; seeing this state of affairs, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> grew enraged.

children.text: तुरँग त्यागि उतरे रणधीरा । लीन सकोप हाथधनुतीरा ॥
children.translated_text: The steadfast warrior dismounted from his horse, and angrily took bow and arrow in hand.

children.text: दो० अतिसकोप कहिवचनकटु छाँड़े विशिख प्रचण्ड ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: With great fury, speaking harsh words, he released fierce arrows.

children.text: कुशबलवंत सो बाणनृप काटि कीन्ह शतखण्ड ॥
children.translated_text: But mighty <s>Kuśa</s> cut those arrows of the king into a hundred pieces.

children.text: लक्ष्मण देखि प्रताप सकाने । आपुते सरिस बीरदोउजाने ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, seeing their prowess, was alarmed — he recognized both as warriors equal to himself.

children.text: दूसर बाण कोपि पुनि मारा । लौकुशबिहँसिकाटिमहिडारा ॥
children.translated_text: He angrily shot another arrow, but <s>Kuśa</s> laughingly cut it down and cast it to the ground.

children.text: होहिंनिफल इमि बाणभवानी । जिमि पाखंडी की हितहानी ॥
children.translated_text: Thus his arrows became futile, O <s>Bhavānī</s>, just as a hypocrite's efforts come to nothing.

children.text: कुशबिलोकिुभूपतिरिसिआना । आपनधनुषश्रवणलगिताना ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Kuśa</s>, seeing the king's rising anger, drew his own bow to its full extent.

children.text: नृप ऊपर बरषा शर कीन्ही । समरसिखावनबहुबिधिदीन्ही ॥
children.translated_text: He showered arrows upon the king and taught him many lessons of battle.

children.text: उत लव सुभट जे भूपतिसंगा । मारिशरनकियेशोणितअंगा ॥
children.translated_text: On the other side, <s>Lava</s> struck the warriors accompanying the king with arrows, bloodying their limbs.

children.text: कहुंभुजमुण्ड कहूं अब रुंडा । धरणिगिरहिंधुनिहोयप्रचंडा ॥
children.translated_text: Here fell severed arms and heads, there headless trunks — they crashed to the ground with tremendous noise.

children.text: बहुत गिरैं बहु उठैं सँभारी । चिघरैं बीर नाद करि भारी ॥
children.translated_text: Many fell, many rose gathering themselves; warriors shrieked, raising great battle-cries.

children.text: बन गिरिखोह नदी नद नारे । शोणित से पूरण भये सारे ॥
children.translated_text: The forests, mountains, caves, rivers, streams, and lakes — all were filled with blood.

children.text: रामाश्वमेध। ४३
children.translated_text: <s>Rāmāśvamedha</s>. 43.

children.text: छन्द ॥
children.translated_text: Chanda:

children.text: सारे नदी नद नार कन्दर खोह शोणितसों भरे ।
children.translated_text: All the rivers, streams, lakes, ravines, and caves were filled with blood.

children.text: कहुं कतहुं वार न पार सूझै सुभट सब घायलपरे ॥
children.translated_text: Nowhere could one see the near or far shore — all warriors lay wounded.

children.text: अधिकारआमिषरुधिर लखिबनजीवसबआयेतहां ।
children.translated_text: Seeing the abundant flesh and blood, all the forest creatures gathered there.

children.text: भरिउदरखाय अघाय जहँतहँ फिरे घरजाकरजहां ॥
children.translated_text: Having filled their bellies and eaten their fill, they roamed here and there, then went to their homes.

children.text: सो० लवनि एक परमान सकल बीर महिमें पस्यो ।
children.translated_text: Sorthā: In but a single moment, <s>Lava</s> laid low all the warriors upon the earth,

children.text: चले जहां प्रियप्रान कुशरणधीर बड़ो अनुज ॥
children.translated_text: and then went to where his beloved elder brother <s>Kuśa</s>, that great warrior, stood in battle.

children.text: लवतहँ आय अनुजपद बन्दे । मिलि सप्रेमदोउबन्धुअनन्दो ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Lava</s> came there and bowed at his elder brother's feet; both brothers met and embraced with love and joy.

children.text: शोभित धनुषबाण युगहाथा । घेस्योआय अनुज रघुनाथा ॥
children.translated_text: Resplendent with bow and arrow in both hands, the younger brother came and surrounded <s>Raghunātha's</s> forces.

children.text: मास्यो बाण बज्र ह्वै लागे । उचकिउचकि घोड़े रथभागे ॥
children.translated_text: He shot arrows that struck like thunderbolts; horses reared and chariots fled.

children.text: घायल भे घोड़े रथटूटे । मातुल मरे पताका छूटे ॥
children.translated_text: Horses were wounded, chariots shattered, generals slain, and banners fell.

children.text: बिरथभये लक्ष्मण खगराई । बूझि न जाय राम प्रभुताई ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, O king of birds, was rendered chariotless — the glory of Lord <s>Rāma</s> is beyond comprehension.

children.text: कहँ लक्ष्मण कहँ वे दोउबीरा । कहँअगस्त्यकहँसिन्धगँभीरा ॥
children.translated_text: Where stands <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and where those two warriors? Where <s>Agastya</s>, and where the deep ocean?

children.text: प्रभु समरत्थ तिहूं यशगावा । असकहियाज्ञवल्क्यशिरनावा ॥
children.translated_text: The Lord is all-capable, praised in all three worlds — so saying, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> bowed his head.

children.text: तब सन्मुख ह्वै कुशललकारा । उठहु सँभरिमहिपालकुमारा ॥
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kuśa</s> faced him and challenged: "Rise and compose yourself, O prince of the earth!

children.text: दूसर रथ मांगौ युवराजा । साजहु सब भूषणरणसाजा ॥
children.translated_text: Ask for another chariot, O crown prince! Array yourself with all ornaments and battle-gear!"

children.text: छन्द ॥
children.translated_text: Chanda:

children.text: संग्राम साज बनाय भूपति सजग ह्वै अब आइये ।
children.translated_text: "Array your battle-gear, O king, be alert and come forth now!

children.text: जाको बिधाता तुरंग दे सो आज रण कर पाइये ॥
children.translated_text: He to whom fate has given the horse — let him claim it today in battle!"

children.text: यहि भांति बारहिंबार जब ललकार कुश बानी कहे ।
children.translated_text: In this manner, again and again, <s>Kuśa</s> issued his challenge with these words.

children.text: सकुचे उषण लखिरिपुबली करि चिन्तवन ठाढ़ेरहे ॥
children.translated_text: Ashamed and seeing the enemy's great strength, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> stood still in anxious thought.

children.text: सो० रहा न धीर खगेश बीर धुरीण अनंत अस ।
children.translated_text: Sorthā: Even that lord of birds, that foremost of warriors, the infinite <s>Śeṣa</s>, could not maintain his composure.

children.text: कौतुक रमारमेश कहाकाग जानैं कवन ॥
children.translated_text: The sport of <s>Ramā</s> and <s>Rameśa</s> — what can <s>Kāka</s> (the crow) know of it, O <s>Bhavānī</s>?

children.text: असकहिकुशलक्ष्मणअनुमाना । बिनमारे मारा तेहिजाना ॥
children.translated_text: Thus speaking, <s>Kuśa</s> reckoned <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> defeated — considered him slain without being slain.

children.text: कछुक सुभट मारे लवबाचे । फिरेते कालशीश जेहिनाचे ॥
children.translated_text: The few warriors that <s>Lava</s> had spared, those upon whose heads Death had danced, they fled.

children.text: कुश सन्मुख आये नियराई । मारि शरनतेहि धरणिसुवाई ॥
children.translated_text: Coming face to face with <s>Kuśa</s>, those who drew near — he struck them with arrows and laid them upon the earth.

children.text: गिरिजासन असकह्यो महेशु ।दुइ क्षौहिणी सुभट सँगशेशू ॥
children.translated_text: O <s>Girijā</s>, thus spoke <s>Maheśa</s>: Two <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s> of warriors were with <s>Śeṣa</s> (i.e., <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>).

children.text: ते लक्ष्मण सारथी समेता । अबलग बाचिरहे रणखेता ॥
children.translated_text: Those warriors along with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and his charioteer had survived on the battlefield until now.

children.text: तब सारथी अपर रथआनी । बहुरि चढ़ेरथ लषणभवानी ॥
children.translated_text: Then the charioteer brought another chariot, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> mounted it once more, O <s>Bhavānī</s>.

children.text: सो अबहोन चहत बिनप्राना । जब कोपैं दोउभट बलवाना ॥
children.translated_text: But now he was about to lose his life, when both mighty warriors attacked in rage.

children.text: प्रभुकारज लखि जो तनुजाई । सबप्रकार मोहिं नेक भलाई ॥
children.translated_text: "If my body perishes in the Lord's service, that is in every way good for me."

children.text: अस उर मंत्र दृढ़ाय भवानी । लषण चले शर शारँगतानी ॥
children.translated_text: Resolving this firmly in his heart, O <s>Bhavānī</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> advanced with arrows set to his <s>Śārṅga</s> bow.

children.text: दो० जबै लषण चढ़ि अपररथ गये जहां दोड बीर ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: When <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> mounted another chariot and went to where the two warriors stood,

children.text: उत्तर प्रतिउत्तर भयो बोले दोउ रण धीर ॥
children.translated_text: challenge and counter-challenge ensued — both warriors, steadfast in battle, spoke.

children.text: मारू परस्पर होय भवानी । दोउ रणधीर बीर अभिमानी ॥
children.translated_text: They attacked each other, O <s>Bhavānī</s> — both steadfast warriors full of pride.

children.text: बाणचले दुहुँदिशि अतितीछे । छेदि अङ्ग निकसे ह्वै पीछे ॥
children.translated_text: Arrows flew from both sides, exceedingly sharp, piercing through limbs and emerging from behind.

children.text: पहरदुइक यहिभांति भवानी । दोउ बीरन रण शंकर ठानी ॥
children.translated_text: For about two <s>paharas</s> (six hours) in this manner, O <s>Bhavānī</s>, both warriors waged a battle worthy of <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: दोउ घायलतन शोणितअंगा । रुधिर प्रवाह बहै सब अंगा ॥
children.translated_text: Both were wounded, their bodies drenched in blood — streams of gore flowed from every limb.

children.text: कुश जान्यो भूपति रण कोपा । मारिशरन तेहिक्षणरथतोपा ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Kuśa</s> perceived the king's fury in battle, and in an instant covered his chariot with arrows.

children.text: जोइ जोइ शरलक्ष्मणबलवाना । घाव करत कुशअंग समाना ॥
children.translated_text: Whatever arrows mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> shot, they were absorbed into <s>Kuśa's</s> body without effect.

children.text: सोइसोइ बाण काटि पट पोंछा । बहुत गहिर बहु लागेओछा ॥
children.translated_text: Each arrow he cut down and wiped away — many struck deep, many grazed lightly.

children.text: यदपि घाव कुश झंझर देहा । तदपि न कुशमन कछुसन्देहा ॥
children.translated_text: Though <s>Kuśa's</s> body was riddled with wounds, still <s>Kuśa</s> harbored no doubt in his heart.

children.text: खींच शरासन शर सान्धाना । बोले गरजि महा बलवाना ॥
children.translated_text: Drawing his bow taut and fitting an arrow, the mighty one roared and spoke:

children.text: दो० सजगहोहु महिपालअब बहुत प्रचारे मोहिं ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: "Be alert now, O king! You have provoked me greatly.

children.text: शप्तमोहिं मुनिपदकमल आजुबधों रणतोहिं ॥
children.translated_text: I swear by the lotus feet of the sage — today I shall slay you in battle!"

children.text: असकहि छांड़े विशिखकराला । लागे तन लक्ष्मण ह्वै काला ॥
children.translated_text: So saying, he released terrible arrows that struck <s>Lakṣmaṇa's</s> body like the coming of Death.

children.text: लागे बाण हृदय अतिकारी । जूझे रण लक्ष्मण बलधारी ॥
children.translated_text: The arrows pierced his heart with great force — mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> fell vanquished in battle.

children.text: मुरछि बिलोकि भूप रणधीरा । निकटगयेकुशलव दोउबीरा ॥
children.translated_text: Seeing the steadfast king fallen unconscious, both brave princes — <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s> — approached.

children.text: देखा निपट कुसाज महीपा । अन्तष्करण बुझानी दीपा ॥
children.translated_text: They saw the king in utter disarray, the lamp of his inner consciousness extinguished.

children.text: तब दोउबन्धु पूजिरणखम्बा । कीनगवनगृहजहँसियअम्बा ॥
children.translated_text: Then both brothers worshipped the victory-pillar of battle and departed for home, where mother <s>Sītā</s> awaited.

children.text: देखा जाय ऋषय फुलवारी । पात पात चहुं ओर निहारी ॥
children.translated_text: Arriving, they beheld the sage's garden and looked all around at every leaf and petal.

children.text: बांधा देख तुरँग मख घोड़ा । भवनचले हियहर्ष न थोड़ा ॥
children.translated_text: Seeing the sacrificial horse tied there, they went toward home with no little joy in their hearts.

children.text: आय मातु पद बन्दि सुखारी । पाय अशीश भयो सुखभारी ॥
children.translated_text: Coming and bowing at their mother's feet with delight, they received her blessings and were filled with happiness.

children.text: घायलसुवन बिलोकिभवानी । जनकसुता तब रोदन ठानी ॥
children.translated_text: Seeing her sons wounded, O <s>Bhavānī</s>, <s>Janaka's</s> daughter began to weep.

children.text: छन्द ॥
children.translated_text: Chanda:

children.text: जब रोदनठानी सियाभवानी बिकलभये बनजीव सुनी ।
children.translated_text: When <s>Sītā</s> began to weep, O <s>Bhavānī</s>, all the forest creatures became distressed upon hearing it.

children.text: धरिविप्र स्वरूपा महाअनूपा आये सब बनदेव तनी ॥
children.translated_text: Assuming the forms of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the supremely beautiful forest deities all came in person.

children.text: धीरजधर अम्बा हे जगदम्बा सुखीरहें दोउ पुत्र सही ।
children.translated_text: "Maintain courage, O Mother, O Mother of the universe — both your sons shall remain well,"

children.text: बहुबिधिसमुझाईकथासुनाई गयेभवन असबातकही ॥
children.translated_text: they consoled her in many ways, narrated tales, and then returned to their abodes, having spoken thus.

children.text: सो० प्रसन देव निजमान श्रमितदेख सियतनय कुल ।
children.translated_text: Sorthā: The forest deities, pleased and of their own accord, seeing <s>Sītā's</s> weary sons' noble lineage,

children.text: करत बचन परमान सदा सर्व अति सुखी तुम ॥
children.translated_text: spoke these words of assurance: "May you always be most happy in all ways."

children.text: इतना कहि बनदेव सिधाई । भैसिय शुद्ध सुवन उरलाई ॥
children.translated_text: Having said this, the forest deities departed; <s>Sītā</s> became calm and embraced her sons to her breast.

children.text: चूमि चाटि अति आदरहेतू । पूँछन लागि कथा रणखेतू ॥
children.translated_text: Kissing and caressing them with great affection, she began asking them the tale of the battlefield.

children.text: जोइ जोइ सियपूछा इतिहासू । सोइसोइ कह्यो न हर्ष हिरासू ॥
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>Sītā</s> asked about the events, they narrated it all, without elation or fear.

children.text: देखि क्षुधित सिय दोऊबारे । दीन मलीन न जाहिं निहारे ॥
children.translated_text: Seeing both her young ones hungry, wretched and forlorn, she could not bear to look at them.

children.text: सूखे बदन लाट मुखलागी । कांपतदेह भूखकी आगी ॥
children.translated_text: Their faces were parched, hair clinging to their cheeks, their bodies trembling with the fire of hunger.

children.text: तुरत उठी लीन्हे करथारी । धरि पकवान लाय महतारी ॥
children.translated_text: She rose at once and took a platter in hand; the mother brought and set out cooked food.

children.text: लागे जेंवन दोऊ भैया । मुदित पियार करै सियमैया ॥
children.translated_text: Both brothers began eating, and Mother <s>Sītā</s>, delighted, showered them with love.

children.text: सुखीभये करि भोजन नाना । नींदबिबशकछुदृगअलसाना ॥
children.translated_text: Having eaten various foods, they became contented; overcome by sleep, their eyes grew drowsy.

children.text: सूते पलंग तुरित दोउभाई । भई सुखी सिय शोच बिहाई ॥
children.translated_text: Both brothers lay down on a bed at once; <s>Sītā</s> became happy, her grief departed.

children.text: दो० यामएक निशिरही जब तबै उठे दोउभ्रात ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: When one watch of the night had passed, then both brothers arose.

children.text: गावेंयश रघुनाथ शुचि जोमन शब्द सुहात ॥
children.translated_text: They sang the glories of <s>Raghunātha</s> in purity — words that delighted the heart.

children.text: सो० सुनि मुनि शुभ इतिहास गूढ़महा यह चरितबर ।
children.translated_text: Sorthā: Hear this auspicious, profound, and great history, O sage,

children.text: शम्भु उमा कैलास कहा कागसन बिहँग तब ॥
children.translated_text: which <s>Śambhu</s> told <s>Umā</s> on <s>Kailāsa</s>, and <s>Kākabhuśuṇḍi</s> then told the bird.

children.text: आगे चरित सुनो गिरिजाई । अतिअगूढ़ नहिंगाय सिराई ॥
children.translated_text: "Hear now the further tale, O daughter of the mountain — it is exceedingly deep and its glory cannot be fully sung.

children.text: थज्ञसभा बैठे रघुराई । भीरबड़ी ऋषि मुनि समुदाई ॥
children.translated_text: In the sacrificial assembly sat <s>Raghurāja</s>, with a great multitude of sages and seers.

children.text: राजनीति अरु वेद पुराना । कहहिं बशिष्ठ करैं सबकाना ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> was expounding statecraft, the <s>Vedas</s>, and the <s>Purāṇas</s>, and all listened attentively.

children.text: सुन्दर जपकर भाग सवाँरैं । पढ़िपढ़िमंत्र अनल महँ डारैं ॥
children.translated_text: They chanted beautiful <s>japas</s> and performed their rites, reciting mantras and casting offerings into the fire.

children.text: तहँ प्रभुकहअसबचनसप्रीती । आयनलषणबहुतदिनबीती ॥
children.translated_text: There the Lord spoke these words with affection: '<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> has not returned, and many days have passed.'

children.text: तेहि अवसर नभते भै बानी । जूझे रणलक्ष्मण हम जानी ॥
children.translated_text: At that moment, a voice came from the sky: 'We know that <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> has fallen in battle.'

children.text: योधा संग बचे नहिंकोऊ । मुरछिपरे मारे उन दोऊ ॥
children.translated_text: 'No warrior who accompanied him has survived; both of those struck him unconscious.'

children.text: एक न बचे सुभट समुदाई । जो यह खबर अवध पहुँचाई ॥
children.translated_text: 'Not a single warrior of the entire host survived to bring this news to <s>Ayodhyā</s>.'

children.text: अजर अमर रण वेदोउबारे । सुभटन तिहुँपुर जीतनहारे ॥
children.translated_text: 'Those two boys are ageless and immortal in battle — warriors capable of conquering the three worlds.'

children.text: सो० बानी सुनत अकाश त्राहि त्राहि कहि लोगसब ।
children.translated_text: Sorthā: Hearing that voice from the sky, all the people cried out 'Alas! Alas!'

children.text: शोचे प्रभु सुखराश उमा दशा सुन अनुज लघु ॥
children.translated_text: The Lord, that ocean of bliss, grieved — O <s>Umā</s>, hear the plight of the younger brother.

children.text: गुरु समीप जोरे दोउहाथा । बोले मधुर वचन रघुनाथा ॥
children.translated_text: Joining both hands before his Guru, <s>Raghunātha</s> spoke sweet words:

children.text: नाथ कहिय जस होय उपाई । करों सोई परमान रजाई ॥
children.translated_text: "Lord, tell me what remedy there may be — I shall do exactly as you command."

children.text: शोचविकल लखिकोशलराया । मुनिनायकबिधिवतसमुझाया ॥
children.translated_text: Seeing the king of <s>Kosala</s> distressed with grief, the chief of sages consoled him with proper counsel:

children.text: नहिं विषाद कर औसर आजू । धीरज धरहु भूप शिरताजू ॥
children.translated_text: "This is not the time for sorrow today. Hold firm your courage, O crown-jewel among kings.

children.text: सैन सवाँरि गवन बन कीजै । कहँ जूझे भाइन सुधि लीजै ॥
children.translated_text: Prepare your army and march to the forest; find where your brother fell and learn the full account."

children.text: लखि आयसु मुनिवर रघुराई । सचिव सुमन्त समीप बुलाई ॥
children.translated_text: Receiving the sage's command, <s>Raghurāja</s> called his minister <s>Sumantra</s> near.

children.text: मख आरंभ पूज हय छाड़े । कीनसुभटतेहिसँगअतिगाढ़े ॥
children.translated_text: "The sacrifice has begun and the horse has been released, and mighty warriors were sent along with it.

children.text: सोहय अबलगफिस्यो न ताता । खेत रहे सँग तीनिहुँ भ्राता ॥
children.translated_text: That horse has not yet returned, dear one — all three brothers remained on the battlefield.

children.text: जाउँ तहां गुरु आयसुदीन्हा । साजहु सैन सचिव परवीना ॥
children.translated_text: I shall go there, as the Guru has commanded — prepare the army, O capable minister."

children.text: दो० लवनि एक परमान मोहिं बीतै कल्प समान ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: "Every single moment feels like an eon to me.

children.text: करिय विलम्ब न तातकछु कीजैबचनप्रमान ॥
children.translated_text: Make no delay at all, dear one — carry out my word as given."

children.text: सुनत सचिव रघुनाथसुबानी । गहिपदविविधभांतिसनमानी ॥
children.translated_text: Hearing the noble words of <s>Raghunātha</s>, the minister grasped his feet and honored him in many ways.

children.text: आयसु नाथ शीशपर लीन्हा । उचितविनयचाहोंकछुकीन्हा ॥
children.translated_text: "I take your command upon my head, my Lord — I wish to make a fitting and humble request.

children.text: जो आयसु पावों रघुराई । तौ कछुकहौं चरण शिरनाई ॥
children.translated_text: If I receive your permission, O <s>Raghurāja</s>, then I shall speak with my head bowed at your feet."

children.text: सचिव विनयसुनिरघुकुलकेता । बोले बचन विवेक समेता ॥
children.translated_text: Hearing the minister's humble plea, the banner of the <s>Raghu</s> dynasty spoke these words of wisdom:

children.text: कहहु तात जो मनअनुमाना । जानों तुम कहँ तातसमाना ॥
children.translated_text: "Speak, dear one, what you have in mind — I regard you as equal to a father."

children.text: मुनि मृदु गूढ़ गिराभगवाना । सचिवसुमन्त चरणलपटाना ॥
children.translated_text: The Lord's gentle and profound speech — minister <s>Sumantra</s> clung to his feet.

children.text: नाथभयो मम उरदुख भारी । सेवक आछत आपुसिधारी ॥
children.translated_text: "Lord, great sorrow has arisen in my heart — while servants remain, the master himself sets forth.

children.text: आयसु होय जाउँ रघुनाथा । जूझे अनुज जहां हयसाथा ॥
children.translated_text: If you command, let me go, O <s>Raghunātha</s>, to where your brother fell, along with the horse.

children.text: जस आज्ञादेइय मोहिंस्वामी । सोई करब चरणअनुगामी ॥
children.translated_text: Whatever order you give me, my Lord, I shall carry it out, ever following in your footsteps."

children.text: सो० सचिववचन सुनिराम बारबार आदर किह्यो ।
children.translated_text: Sorthā: Hearing the minister's words, <s>Rāma</s> honored him again and again.

children.text: तुम सबपूरण काम रहहु अवध असरामकहि ॥
children.translated_text: "You are accomplished in all things — remain in <s>Ayodhyā</s>," thus spoke <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: मैं अब जाउँ वहां सुनुताता । देखों जाय दशा सब भ्राता ॥
children.translated_text: "I shall now go there myself, listen dear one — I shall go and see the state of all my brothers.

children.text: को अस बीर भयो जगभारी । जो रणखेत अनुज सबमारी ॥
children.translated_text: Who is this mighty warrior that has appeared in the world, who has slain all my brothers on the battlefield?

children.text: देखहुं कौन द्वीप सों आयो । जो बनमें अस रारिमचायो ॥
children.translated_text: Let me see from which land he has come, who has stirred up such a quarrel in the forest.

children.text: जो मुनितनय तो कीनकुचाली । जो पै भूप तो प्रणप्रतिपाली ॥
children.translated_text: If they are sage's sons, then they have acted wickedly; if they are princes, then they are guardians of honor."

children.text: देखि सचिवरुख दीनदयाला । तुरत गयोजहँ हयगयशाला ॥
children.translated_text: Seeing the minister's demeanor, the compassionate Lord went at once to where the horse-stable was.

children.text: साजहुतुरंग मतंग अतिभारी । रथ सुखपाल विमानसवाँरी ॥
children.translated_text: "Prepare the horses and mighty elephants, the chariots, palanquins, and aerial conveyances!"

children.text: फिरे दूत कोशलपुर खोरी । भेभट सजगहरष नहिंथोरी ॥
children.translated_text: Messengers returned swiftly to <s>Kosalapura</s>; the warriors became alert and felt no small delight.

children.text: साजि समर हथियार भवानी । भे यकठौर न जाय बखानी ॥
children.translated_text: Arming themselves with battle weapons, O <s>Bhavānī</s>, they assembled at one place — it is beyond description.

children.text: दो० तब सुमन्तपदकमल प्रभु गहे जोरियुग पानि ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: Then <s>Sumantra</s> grasped the lotus feet of the Lord, joining both his hands.

children.text: भईतयारी सैनप्रभु अस कहि विविधबखानि ॥
children.translated_text: "The army is prepared, O Lord" — thus he spoke with various expressions of respect.

children.text: नित्य क्रिया करि तब रघुराई । पूजि महेश मुदित शिरनाई ॥
children.translated_text: Having performed the daily rituals, <s>Raghurāī</s> (Lord of the <s>Raghus</s>) then joyfully bowed his head and worshipped <s>Maheśa</s> (Lord <s>Śiva</s>).

children.text: गजरथचढ़ि रघुनाथ मुनीशा । बोलिसुमन्त कह्यो अवधेशा ॥
children.translated_text: Mounting the elephant-chariot, <s>Raghunātha</s> and the chief sage — <s>Sumanta</s> was called, and <s>Avadhēśa</s> (Lord of <s>Ayodhyā</s>) spoke:

children.text: राखब रुख मुनिनायक केरी । जो मुनि कहैं सो करब न बेरी ॥
children.translated_text: 'We shall respect the wishes of the chief among sages; whatever the sage says, we shall do without delay.'

children.text: करि आगे सब सुभट भवानी । हांक्योरथ मातुलरुख जानी ॥
children.translated_text: Placing all the warriors ahead, O <s>Bhavānī</s>, he drove the chariot forward, knowing his uncle's intent.

children.text: चले साथ अङ्गद हनुबीरा । जामवन्त योधा रणधीरा ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Aṅgada</s> and <s>Hanubīrā</s> (the valiant <s>Hanumān</s>) went along, with <s>Jāmavanta</s> and other warriors, steadfast in battle.

children.text: चलत राम बहुशकुन सुहाई । को कहिस कै बीर समुदाई ॥
children.translated_text: As <s>Rāma</s> set forth, many auspicious omens appeared — who can describe that assembly of heroes?

children.text: आश्रम बालमीकि नियराई । देखि टेढ़बन सुभट डराई ॥
children.translated_text: As they neared <s>Vālmīki's</s> hermitage, the warriors were frightened seeing the dense, twisted forest.

children.text: धायखात जिमिकाल कराला । ठौकैं केहरि बिबिध बिशाला ॥
children.translated_text: Trenches and pits like the gaping jaws of <s>Kāla</s> (Death), and lions of many kinds, massive, prowling everywhere.

children.text: देखि विपिन नहिं धीरज होई । यह बन कहोजाय किमिकोई ॥
children.translated_text: Seeing the forest, no one could maintain courage — 'How can anyone enter this forest?' they said.

children.text: सो० लखि बन महागँभीर परै न आगे पाऊँ कोउ ।
children.translated_text: Sohā: Seeing the vast, profound forest, no one could set foot forward.

children.text: कृपासिन्धु रघुबीर बोलि सुभटअस बचनकह ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Raghubīra</s> (the heroic <s>Rāma</s>), ocean of mercy, called the warriors and spoke these words:

children.text: धीरजधरि पैठो बन माहीं । बनचर लोग न कोउसमुहाहीं ॥
children.translated_text: 'Take courage and enter the forest — do not confront the forest-dwelling people.

children.text: खोजहु तुरंग डरहुजनिकाहू । भयतजिसकलबिपिनमहँजाहू ॥
children.translated_text: Search for the horse, fear no one; abandoning fear, go everywhere throughout the forest.

children.text: पावोखोज जहां मखबाजू । आनहु बेगि न होय अकाजू ॥
children.translated_text: Find and search where the sacrificial horse is; bring it quickly, lest misfortune befall us.'

children.text: सुनिआयसु जहँतहँ कटकाई । कीन प्रवेश तुरित बन जाई ॥
children.translated_text: Hearing the command, the army entered swiftly, going into the forest from all sides.

children.text: खोजनलागे तुरंग मुनीशा । योधामहँ भट सँग अवधेशा ॥
children.translated_text: They began searching for the horse, O chief sage — warriors and soldiers along with the Lord of <s>Ayodhyā</s>.

children.text: नदी खोह गिरि कन्दरभारी । पातपात बन सकल निहारी ॥
children.translated_text: Rivers, ravines, mountains, and great caves — they surveyed every part of every forest.

children.text: पग पग शोधत सुभटसयाने । जाहिं चलेबन सघन समाने ॥
children.translated_text: Step by step the wise warriors searched, advancing into the dense, impenetrable forest.

children.text: फिरहिं सुभट बनमें सबधावा । खोज तुरंग काहू नहिं पावा ॥
children.translated_text: The warriors roamed through the entire forest in every direction, but none found any trace of the horse.

children.text: सुनि मुनिवरब्याकुल कटकाई । देख्यो फिरत एक अमराई ॥
children.translated_text: The anxious army heard of a sage's presence, and while wandering, spotted a mango grove.

children.text: दो० तहांबाजि मखदेख तिन खड़े सुवन दुइ चार ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: There they saw the sacrificial horse standing, with two or four young boys nearby.

children.text: बोले सुभट बिनीततब मुनिबालकन निहार ॥
children.translated_text: The warriors then spoke humbly, beholding the sage's children:

children.text: सा० सुनहु तनय मुनिराय सुन्दर बाजि अनूप अति ।
children.translated_text: Sohā: 'Listen, O sons of the sage-king — this horse is exceedingly beautiful and matchless.

children.text: कहि नरेश सों जाय लीनेहु मांगि तुरंग यह ॥
children.translated_text: Go and tell the king, and obtain this horse by asking him.'

children.text: सुनि यह वचन तुरंग रखवारे । उठे सकोपि नयन अरुणारे ॥
children.translated_text: Hearing these words, the guardians of the horse rose up in anger, their eyes reddened.

children.text: बोल्यो उचित सुनों यह भीरा । तुम केहि हेतु फिरो बनबीरा ॥
children.translated_text: One spoke fittingly: 'Listen, you crowd — for what purpose do you wander in the forest, O warriors?

children.text: निज भुज बल हम लीन तुरंगा । मारे अमित अनीचतुरंगा ॥
children.translated_text: By the strength of our own arms we captured this horse, and slew countless soldiers of the wicked army.

children.text: सो तुम कहत कि गायवजाई । कोउ नरेशहि लीन रिझाई ॥
children.translated_text: Yet you say we should go like cattle, that someone has taken it to please the king?

children.text: अस सन्देह तो लेहु लड़ाई । ईश देय सो लेय बड़ाई ॥
children.translated_text: If you have such doubts, then take up battle — whoever God grants, let him take the glory.'

children.text: वचन परस्पर सुन सुनगाढ़े । रहे दोउ कुवँर उमा कहुँठाढ़े ॥
children.translated_text: Hearing increasingly harsh words exchanged, O <s>Umā</s>, the two princes stood firm.

children.text: धाये साजि शरासन बाना । परम धीर दोऊ बलवाना ॥
children.translated_text: They rushed forward, readying their bows and arrows — both supremely brave and mighty.

children.text: भीर देखि मुनिवर फुलवाई । आये सीध तहां दोउ भाई ॥
children.translated_text: Seeing the commotion, the sage's sons in the garden came straight to that place, both brothers.

children.text: रखवारेन की संकट देखी । उठेतमकि दोउ कुवँरविशेखी ॥
children.translated_text: Seeing the distress of the guardians, the two distinguished princes rose up in fury.

children.text: छन्द ॥
children.translated_text: Verse:

children.text: भाक्रोध दोउरणधीरमुनिवर चापशरकर सोहई ।
children.translated_text: The two battle-steadfast sage-sons, wrathful, looked splendid with bow and arrow in hand,

children.text: नखशिखअनेक मयंकशोभाकामरति लखिमोहई ॥
children.translated_text: From head to toe, their beauty like countless moons — even <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love) and <s>Rati</s> were enchanted seeing them.

children.text: बोले सकोप बिलोकयोधा तुरितसन्मुख जायकै ।
children.translated_text: They spoke angrily, looking at the warriors, and went forward swiftly to confront them:

children.text: असकौन कीन्ह अनीत मूढ़हु बाग घेरेहु आयकै ॥
children.translated_text: 'Who among you committed this injustice, O fools — you have come and surrounded the garden!

children.text: तजिबागजाहु परायजहँतहँ जो भलाअपनाचहहु ।
children.translated_text: Leave the garden and go away wherever you came from, if you wish your own well-being.

children.text: नहिं होहु सकल पतङ्गदीपक जो इहां ठाढ़े रहहु ॥
children.translated_text: If you remain standing here, you shall all become moths to a flame.'

children.text: असकहि बहुरिकुश धनुचढ़ाये विषमशरजोरतभये ।
children.translated_text: Saying this, <s>Kuśa</s> strung his bow again and began fitting fearsome arrows.

children.text: सिमटेसुभटलखिअतुलबलमुनिबागतजिबाहरगये ॥
children.translated_text: The warriors shrank back seeing his unmatched strength, and left the sage's garden.

children.text: सो० त्यागि सुभट मुनिबाग खड़ेभये मैदान लखि ।
children.translated_text: Sohā: The warriors abandoned the sage's garden and stood in the open field.

children.text: बचनबाणसम लाग कछुकगये निजनाथपहँ ॥
children.translated_text: Their words struck like arrows; some of them went to their own lord.

children.text: नायशीश प्रभुचरण भवानी । कथासकलमखअश्वबखानी ॥
children.translated_text: Bowing their heads at the Lord's feet, O <s>Bhavānī</s>, they narrated the entire story of the sacrificial horse.

children.text: नाथ बिपिनमहँ बाग मुनीशा । बांधा तुरग तहां जगदीशा ॥
children.translated_text: 'Lord, in the forest there is a sage's garden; the horse has been tied there, O Lord of the Universe.

children.text: सुवन घने ऋषि मुनिबरदेवा । हाथों हाथ करैं हय सेवा ॥
children.translated_text: Dense trees, sages, and holy men — they are tending the horse with their own hands.

children.text: घेरा बाग जहां मख घोरा । रखवारन तब कीन्ह्यो शोरा ॥
children.translated_text: The garden where the sacrificial horse is has been surrounded; the guardians then raised an alarm.

children.text: त्यहि अवसर दुइ कुँवर अनोखे । शोर सुनत कतहूँ अतिचोखे ॥
children.translated_text: At that moment, two extraordinary princes — hearing the commotion from somewhere, exceedingly keen —

children.text: रूपराशि सुठि अङ्घ सुहाई । बिधिअसछबिनहिंसकैबनाई ॥
children.translated_text: Treasures of beauty, with perfectly lovely limbs — even <s>Brahmā</s> could not fashion such splendor.

children.text: उपमा नहिं त्रिभुवनमाँ कोऊ । जस सुन्दर मुनिबालक दोऊ ॥
children.translated_text: There is no comparison in the three worlds — so handsome are those two sage-boys.

children.text: कर शरविषम तूणिकटि बांधे । मैनचाप शोभित अति कांधे ॥
children.translated_text: Fearsome arrows in hand, quivers tied at the waist, great bows adorning their shoulders.

children.text: देखत छोट महा बलधामा । जीति सकै को करि संग्रामा ॥
children.translated_text: Though small in appearance, they are abodes of great strength — who could defeat them in battle?'

children.text: दो० बयकिशोर सुखमा सदन कोटिकाम छबि लाज ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: Of adolescent age, abodes of beauty, putting the splendor of ten million <s>Kāmadevas</s> to shame,

children.text: सिंहनाद लौं शब्दकर आप तहां मखबाजा ॥
children.translated_text: with a roar like a lion's cry, they themselves came there to the sacrificial horse.

children.text: ताके भय सब सुभट डराई । भे बाहर तजि मुनि फुलवाई ॥
children.translated_text: Out of fear of them, all the warriors fled in fright, leaving the sage's garden.

children.text: समिट ठाढ़भे लखि मैदानू । भयो क्रोध जनु प्रबल कृशानू ॥
children.translated_text: They gathered and stood upon seeing the open field; their anger blazed like a mighty fire.

children.text: होन चहत संग्राम अपारा । प्रभुआयसुजस होय तुम्हारा ॥
children.translated_text: 'A great battle is about to commence — whatever the Lord commands, so be it, sire.'

children.text: बोले तब कृपालु रघुराई । मिलै तुरग सो करहु उपाई ॥
children.translated_text: Then the gracious <s>Raghurāī</s> spoke: 'Devise a plan to recover the horse.

children.text: इतनाकहि कटिकस्यो निषङ्गा । लीन्ह्यो हाथ कठिन शारङ्गा ॥
children.translated_text: Saying this, he fastened the quiver to his waist and took the mighty bow <s>Śārṅga</s> in hand.

children.text: शीशनाय महिदेव मुनेशा । चढ़े तुरग तिहुँलोक नरेशा ॥
children.translated_text: Bowing his head to the Brahmins and sages, the Lord of the Three Worlds mounted his horse.

children.text: बिपिनप्रवेश कीन सियरवनू । साथऋषभअंगद सुतपवनू ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Siyaravanu</s> (<s>Rāma</s>, husband of <s>Sītā</s>) entered the forest, accompanied by <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Aṅgada</s>, and the son of <s>Pavana</s> (<s>Hanumān</s>).

children.text: मुरछित बीर परे रणमाहीं । पगभर पन्थमिलै कहुँ नाहीं ॥
children.translated_text: Unconscious warriors lay on the battlefield; not a soul could be found on the path.

children.text: भरत लुषण रिपुदमन समेतू । सुभट सहित रण परे अचेतू ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and <s>Ripudamana</s> together — the warriors lay senseless on the battlefield.

children.text: सो० उमासुनोचितलाय याज्ञवल्क्य यह शुभचरित ।
children.translated_text: Sohā: Listen, O <s>Umā</s>, with due attention — <s>Yājñavalkya</s> narrates this auspicious tale,

children.text: भरद्वाज प्रति गाय बायसनाथ खगेश ते ॥
children.translated_text: which <s>Bharadvāja</s> sings, received from <s>Kākanātha</s> (<s>Bhuśuṇḍi</s>), the lord of birds.

children.text: सुनि रघुबर इतिहास अनूपा । सुनहु सुता हेमञ्चल भूप ॥
children.translated_text: 'Hear the matchless history of the best of the <s>Raghus</s>, O daughter' — thus spoke King <s>Hemañcala</s> (the <s>Himālaya</s>).

children.text: हरनशोक संशय तम भारी । अरु चितचाव बढ़ावनहारी ॥
children.translated_text: 'It destroys grief and the darkness of doubt, and increases the delight of the heart.

children.text: व्यापक ब्रह्म चराचर स्वामी । सुरनरअसुर जासु अनुगामी ॥
children.translated_text: The all-pervading <s>Brahman</s>, lord of all moving and unmoving beings, followed by gods, men, and demons,

children.text: अविगत अविनाशी निष्कामा । स्वइ मम इष्ट उमा सियरामा ॥
children.translated_text: unknowable, imperishable, desireless — O <s>Umā</s>, my own beloved deity is <s>Siyarāma</s> (<s>Sītā</s> and <s>Rāma</s>).'

children.text: असकहि कामधेनु शिरनावा । देखि दशा गिरिजा सुखपावा ।
children.translated_text: Saying thus, <s>Kāmadhenu</s> (the divine cow) bowed her head; seeing the state of affairs, <s>Girijā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>) was pleased.

children.text: लागे बहुरि कहन वृषकेतू । ज्यहिबिधि रामगये रणखेतू ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛṣaketu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) began to narrate again — how <s>Rāma</s> went to the battlefield.

children.text: दशा अनुज अवलोकि भवानी । लखि रघुबीर अचम्भवमानी ॥
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhavānī</s>, seeing the condition of his younger brothers, <s>Raghubīra</s> was filled with astonishment.

children.text: बोले बोलि समीर कुमारा । बिधिगतितातनजायविचारा ॥
children.translated_text: He called <s>Samīra Kumāra</s> (<s>Hanumān</s>, son of the Wind) and said: 'The workings of Fate cannot be fathomed, son.

children.text: कहँ रिपुदमन सुभट रणधीरा । कहँ वे मुनि किशोर दोउवीरा ॥
children.translated_text: Where is <s>Ripudamana</s>, that warrior steadfast in battle? And where are those two heroic sage-boys?'

children.text: सो० बयकिशोर दोउबार कहँ रिपुसूदन अजरभट ।
children.translated_text: Sohā: 'Those two boys of tender age — and where is <s>Ripusūdana</s>, the invincible warrior?

children.text: अचरज पवन कुमार कहै कवन बूझे कवन ॥
children.translated_text: It is astonishing, O son of the Wind — who can explain it, who can comprehend it?'

children.text: दो० उमा करत नर यों चरित धरे मनुष्य कृपाल ।
children.translated_text: Dohā: O <s>Umā</s>, thus does the gracious Lord enact human deeds, having assumed a human form.

children.text: निरखिदशारिपुदमनभटभयेबिकलत्यहिकाल ॥
children.translated_text: Seeing the condition of <s>Ripudamana</s> and the warriors, he was deeply distressed at that time.

children.text: आगे चले राम रणधीरा । मुरछित बिपिनदेखिसबबीरा ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, steadfast in battle, moved ahead, seeing all the warriors lying unconscious in the forest.

children.text: कोउ कहरैं कोउ मांगैं बारी । कोउ घुमरैं कोउ उठैं सँभारी ॥
children.translated_text: Some lay groaning, some cried for water; some were dazed, some rose up, steadying themselves.

children.text: धरुधरु मारू पुकारैं कोऊ । कोउ उसकैं मूँदे दृग दोऊ ॥
children.translated_text: 'Seize them! Strike them!' some cried out; some gasped, closing both eyes.

children.text: देखाजाय भरत गति आगे । परे मुरछि रथपर शरलागे ॥
children.translated_text: Going ahead, he saw <s>Bharata's</s> condition — lying unconscious on his chariot, pierced by arrows.

children.text: भरे अन्तशर चाप निषंगा । बाणनते बेधे सब अंग। ॥
children.translated_text: His body was filled with arrows, bow and quiver full of shafts — arrows had pierced every limb.

children.text: बीर धुरीण भरत जगलीका । साधु सभासुरमुनिमहँ टीका ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s>, the foremost among heroes, the pillar of the world, the crown jewel among saintly assemblies, gods, and sages —

children.text: ते अवगतिकर सुवन मुनीशा । सोवत समरभूमि धरिशीशा ॥
children.translated_text: those sons of the sage had reduced him to such a state; he lay on the battlefield with his head bowed.

children.text: देखी कस वे ऋषय कुमारे । जो अगणित सेना रणमारे ॥
children.translated_text: 'How were those sage-boys, who slew countless armies in battle?

children.text: लखिकरतूति तासु मन शोचू । कहत तात उर होत सकोचू ॥
children.translated_text: Seeing their deeds fills my mind with sorrow; saying this, O father, the heart is overwhelmed with anguish.'

children.text: सो० कहां भरत रणधीर कहँ वे युगलकिशोर मुनि ।
children.translated_text: Sohā: 'Where is <s>Bharata</s>, steadfast in battle, and where are those two young sage-boys?

children.text: समुझततनय समीर ज्ञानिहु होतबिमोहबश ॥
children.translated_text: Reflect upon it, O son of the Wind — even the wise are overcome with bewilderment.'

children.text: असकहि रामचले मुनिराया । जाको सपन्यहु मोह न माया ॥
children.translated_text: Saying this, <s>Rāma</s> proceeded, O sage — he whom not even a dream can touch with delusion or illusion.

children.text: नर अनुहार चरितकर सोई । पोषण भरण विश्वकर जोई ॥
children.translated_text: He who enacts deeds in human fashion — he who nourishes and sustains the entire universe.

children.text: चला तुरग आयो मुनि तहँवाँ । मुरछित लषणपरे रण जहँवाँ ॥
children.translated_text: The horse went forward, and the sage came to that place where <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> lay unconscious on the battlefield.

children.text: जबरघुकुलमणिअनुज निहारी । नयन स्रवतजल रामखरारी ॥
children.translated_text: When the jewel of the <s>Raghu</s> dynasty saw his younger brother, tears streamed from <s>Rāma's</s> eyes, slayer of <s>Khara</s>.

children.text: सुभट समेत समर महँ सोई । शरन पूर तन न जोई ॥
children.translated_text: Together with the warriors on the battlefield — his body so full of arrows it could not be recognized.

children.text: जे अनन्त धननादहि मारी । ते दोउ मुनिबालकन सँहारी ॥
children.translated_text: Those who had slain <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Dhana</s>, and <s>Nāda</s> — those two sage-boys had vanquished them.

children.text: असअनरथबिधिकहँनहिंशोभा । चरितबिलोकिमोरमनक्षोभा ॥
children.translated_text: 'Such calamity does not befit <s>Brahmā's</s> design; beholding these events, my mind is agitated.

children.text: कहत वचन भरमर जलनयना । सुनहुमुनीश रामसुखअयना ॥
children.translated_text: Speaking these words, tears streaming from his eyes like bees from flowers — hear, O chief sage, <s>Rāma</s>, the abode of bliss.'

children.text: सो० यथामीन जलहीन परे जाल तलफै परी ॥
children.translated_text: Sohā: Just as a fish, bereft of water, fallen into a net, writhes and gasps,

children.text: लक्ष्मण तथा मलीन यदपि उमा गाढ़े सुभट ॥
children.translated_text: so too <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> lay wretched — though, O <s>Umā</s>, he was a mighty warrior.

children.text: दो० देखि बिपिन संग्राम महि शीलटसिन्धु सुखधाम ।
